dedupe_keys.name: datacentergym physics grounded simulator for multi objective scheduling across geo distributed data centres

description: DataCenterGym is a simulation environment for job scheduling in geo-distributed data centres that couples compute queueing, building thermal dynamics, localised HVAC behaviour and temperature-dependent service degradation behind a Gymnasium-compatible interface, designed as a reusable testbed. The paper motivates it by noting that most schedulers treat compute utilisation, heat generation, cooling demand and energy use independently, although they are tightly coupled, and also develops a Hierarchical Model Predictive Control scheduling algorithm that places jobs while accounting for thermal and power dynamics; experiments on nominal operation and workload sensitivity show it improving on baseline schedulers. Producer: Nilavra Pathak, Samadrita Biswas and Nirmalya Roy; first submitted on 17 April 2026 (ten pages, five figures) and published at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Smart Computing. Coverage: generic geo-distributed data centres. Access: the abstract page gives the paper only; a code release was not confirmed, so open_source is recorded as false, meaning no verified open-source release. Licence and cost: not stated for the software; the paper is free and it is under the CC-BY-4.0. Caveats: results come from the authors' experiments, and the site parameters used were not read here. Simulation uses: it supports optimisation and capacity-planning studies of how scheduling, cooling and power interact. Related record: CERF-DC, the data centre geospatial siting and cost package (model-cerf-dc-data-centre-geospatial-siting-costs).
